html:
After the Cuban Revolution of 1959, over a million Cubans left their island, most for the United States. The first to go were the middle and upper classes whose property was seized.

Waves followed: Freedom Flights from 1965 to 1973, the Mariel boatlift of 1980, the rafters of 1994 during the Special Period, and new departures in the 2020s. A US law of 1966 gave Cubans an easy path to residence.

The exiles turned Miami into a bilingual city and a business centre for Latin America. Cuban Americans became a strong voice in US politics, backing the embargo. Families split by the Florida Straits are a lasting part of Cuban life.
